Kaohsiung family falls ill from eating wild mushrooms
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-22
16:45:57 UTC
01:45:57 KST

The Kaohsiung Department of Health yesterday urged people not to eat wild mushrooms, as it reported that a family had sought hospital treatment after reportedly eating unidentified mushrooms picked in a grassland.
High temperatures and rainfall in the south made it easier for poisonous mushrooms to grow in grasslands, the department said.
A hospital on Friday reported that a family of three had sought emergency treatment for symptoms including vomiting, diarrhea and headaches after reportedly eating wild white mushrooms.
Photo courtesy of a member of the public
The family on Thursday evening cooked unidentified mushrooms that a friend had picked in a grassland and given to them. Later that night, they began experiencing symptoms of food poisoning and sought treatment. One family member was hospitalized due to severe symptoms, the department said.
The department said some poisonous mushrooms look similar to edible mushrooms, making it difficult for members of the public to identify them safely based only on appearance, color or comparisons with online images.
The “green-spored parasol” is commonly found in Taiwan and is one of the poisonous mushrooms frequently eaten by mistake, it said, adding that it is medium to large in size and often found in open outdoor spaces at low elevations and on Taiwan’s plains.
Its gills are initially white, turning greenish-yellow or grayish-green as it matures, and it can easily be confused with edible species such as the parasol mushroom (Macrolepiota procera) or the termite mushroom (Termitomyces eurrhizus), it added.
Accidental ingestion can cause intense gastrointestinal distress within one to three hours, with common symptoms including nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, diarrhea, bloody stool and dehydration, the department said.
The severity of symptoms can vary depending on a person’s condition and the amount consumed, but anyone who accidentally ingests a wild mushroom or feels unwell after eating one should seek medical attention as soon as possible, it said.
People should remember never to pick, cook or eat unknown wild mushrooms to prevent food poisoning, it added.
Separately, the Penghu County Health Bureau last month urged the public to avoid picking or eating wild plants and mushrooms or giving or receiving them as gifts, and to be mindful of the sources of food ingredients and their storage conditions.
It also promoted its “five do’s and two don’ts” principle for preventing food poisoning: people should wash their hands before handling food, choose fresh food ingredients, keep raw and cooked food separate, cook food thoroughly, store food in appropriate temperatures, and should not drink unpurified mountain spring water or pick and eat wild plants and animals.

As Europe rearms, Italy’s  space sector faces a scale test
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-22
16:45:56 UTC
01:45:56 KST

Italy’s fragmented space industry is facing growing pressure to consolidate as defense and government customers increasingly favor larger suppliers capable of handling complex programs.
The shift reflects a broader push across Europe to build strategic autonomy in defense and critical technologies, as governments respond to Russia’s invasion of Ukraine, tensions with China and uncertainty over future US security commitments.
For Italy, whose space sector is known for niche engineering expertise, but remains dominated by small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), the challenge is whether firms can build the scale and financial strength needed to compete for large contracts without losing their flexibility.
Photo: Bloomberg
Limited access to capital remains a major obstacle, industry executives say.
“In Italy, we used to say: ‘Small is beautiful,’ but that’s not true,” said Alessandro Franzoni, CEO of optical instrumentation specialist Officina Stellare.
Leonardo, Italy’s largest aerospace and defense company, said new projects require integrated technological capabilities, industrial reliability and the capacity to manage growing complexity.
“When selecting and developing its supply chain, the group favors suppliers capable of offering solid expertise, production capacity, resilience and operational continuity,” a spokesperson said.
Satellite navigation and cybersecurity specialist Qascom said customers now expect suppliers to provide products, hardware and industrial capabilities, not just engineering know-how.
“You need to grow, because remaining small doesn’t work,” cofounder and CEO Alessandro Pozzobon said.
The pressure has intensified as Europe’s space sector becomes more closely tied to defense and security priorities.
Europe’s defense build-up and growing demand for dual-use technologies, which can serve civilian and military purposes, have increased the importance of resilient industrial capacity.
The rise of Elon Musk’s SpaceX has also highlighted the advantages of scale, vertical integration and access to capital enjoyed by larger industry players.
“I see a trend towards aggregation, driven by the market,” said Giuseppe Acierno, president of the DTA aerospace hub in Apulia, southern Italy. “It is a trend that should be supported.”
Renato Panesi, chief commercial officer at Italian space logistics company D-Orbit, said Europe remains disadvantaged by fragmented programs and weaker access to private funding than the US.
Yet consolidation brings risks. Qascom said much of Italy’s fragmentation reflects deep technological specialization, with smaller firms occupying globally competitive niches in navigation, cybersecurity and advanced communications.
The challenge is finding ways to build scale without sacrificing innovation, executives said.
Building larger companies would require funding.
Last month, Intesa Sanpaolo, the European Investment Bank and the European Space Agency (ESA) launched a program expected to provide up to 300 million euros (US$350.3 million) in financing for aerospace SMEs.
“For too many of our space SMEs, the barrier to growth is not technology, but access to capital,” ESA Director General Josef Aschbacher said.
The Italian Interministerial Committee for Space and Aerospace Research Policies estimated the country’s aerospace sector would receive 7.8 billion euros in investment and program funding by 2028, including 3.5 billion euros linked to Italy’s contribution to ESA programs.
For some companies, acquisitions have become the quickest route to achieving the scale customers demand.
Officina Stellare merged with Global Aerospace Technologies Group in June, creating an aerospace and defense platform with a pro-forma order backlog of 192 million euros.
Franzoni said the deal was designed to combine complementary technologies, strengthen vertical integration and broaden the group’s offering.
“I see now an opportunity, mostly in Italy, for further aggregation. We are looking for synergies for technologies and for production synergies,” he said.
Officina Stellare reinforced that strategy last month through the acquisition of electric motor specialist Mavel.
D-Orbit has also expanded through acquisitions, buying Earth observation specialist Planetek before raising fresh capital to fund further deals.
“The driver of our M&A [mergers and acquisitions] strategy is the acquisition of additional capabilities and services to offer to government, defense and commercial satellite operators,” Panesi said.
Recent contracts appear to reflect the shift. Officina Stellare this month secured a 6.5 million euro contract from Leonardo for optical communications terminals and another worth more than 7 million euros from the Italian Space Agency for an Earth observation program.
The company said the awards showed its ability to move beyond technology development and deliver integrated systems at industrial scale.
For industry executives, the question is no longer whether Italy’s space companies need to grow.
It is whether a sector built on specialized SMEs can secure the capital and scale needed to compete in a changing European market before competitors, or foreign acquirers, do it for them.

While some healing economy trends focus on comforting products, others take the form of experiences. One recent example is puppy yoga, a class in which participants practice yoga as puppies wander freely around the room. The idea is simple: while people move through yoga poses, the presence of playful puppies is meant to create a joyful and relaxing atmosphere. Supporters claim the classes provide stress relief for humans. At the same time, they also help the dogs socialize with people.
Photo: AdobeStock I 照片: AdobeStock
However, animal welfare experts have raised serious concerns about this trend. Some investigations have reported that puppies as young as six weeks old are used in these classes. Puppies should normally remain with their mothers for at least eight weeks to develop properly. Instead, they may spend hours in busy rooms filled with unfamiliar people.
Such environments can be overwhelming for young puppies. At this age, they need a sense of safety and the presence of a familiar caregiver when they are introduced to new experiences. Without this support, stressful situations may negatively affect their emotional and behavioral development.
For this reason, puppy yoga raises an important question about the healing economy. Although many wellness trends promise comfort and happiness for people, they may also create ethical concerns about how animals are treated.
有些療癒經濟趨勢著重在療癒人心的商品，其他則是體驗的形式。近期的一個例子是小狗瑜伽，在這樣的課程裡，參加者會在幼犬自由漫步於教室內的情況下練瑜伽。這個想法很簡單：當人們在做不同的瑜伽動作時，有愛玩的幼犬在場是為了打造歡樂又放鬆的氣氛。支持者宣稱這些課程能為人們提供壓力的紓解。同時，也有助於狗狗與人類互動。
然而，動物福利專家對這股趨勢提出高度疑慮。一些調查指出，這些課程中使用的幼犬年齡甚至只有六週大。幼犬通常應該與犬媽媽待到至少八週才能正常發育。牠們卻可能在充滿陌生人的忙碌教室裡待上好幾個小時。
這樣的環境對幼犬來說可能難以負荷。在這個年齡段，當牠們接觸新事物時，需要安全感以及熟悉照顧者的陪伴。若缺乏這樣的支持，充滿壓力的情況可能會對牠們的情緒與行為發展造成負面影響。
因此，狗狗瑜伽帶出了一個與療癒經濟相關的重要問題。儘管許多健康療癒的趨勢承諾能為人們帶來慰藉與快樂，但同時也可能引發如何對待動物的倫理疑慮。
What Did You Learn?
1-2. 請從第二天文章中找出最適當的單詞填入下列句子空格中，並視句型結構需要做適當的字形變化，使句子語意完整、語法正確，並符合全文文意。每格限填一個單詞（word）。（填充題）
Puppy yoga supposedly provides human relaxation and opportunities for dog __1__ with humans. However, experts warn that early introduction to busy environments without a safe caregiver hinders the puppies’ proper development and raises questions about the __2__ of using animals.
答案:1. socialization 2. ethics
3. From (A) to (F) below, choose the ONES that are true for both JellyCat and puppy yoga.（多選題）
(A) They both involve direct interactions with animals.
(B) They are promoted through videos on social media platforms.
(C) They show how businesses respond to people’s emotional needs.
(D) They both have sparked discussions about their possible negative effects.
(E) They are mainly intended to improve animals’ well-being and development.
(F) They reflect a growing interest in products or activities that support mental well-being.
答案:C、F
Words in Use
1. participant n. 參與者
Each participant in the marathon will receive a medal after they complete the race.
馬拉松賽事的每位參與者在完賽後都會收到一枚獎牌。
2. wander vi. 漫遊，閒晃
Holly wandered through the narrow streets of the old town.
荷莉在舊城區的狹窄街道上漫步。
3. presence n. 在場，存在
The judge requested the presence of a translator for the foreign witness.
法官要求為外籍證人安排一名翻譯員在場。
4. atmosphere n. 氣氛，氛圍
The live music added a festive atmosphere to the outdoor market.
現場音樂為戶外市集增添了節慶的氣氛。
5. socialize vi. 社交，交際
socialize with... 與……社交
Ken is socializing with the other hikers while they rest by the lake.
在湖邊休息時，阿肯與其他登山客交流互動。
Practical Phrases
1. be meant to V 意在（做）……
These exercises are meant to strengthen the lower back muscles.
這些運動意在強化下背肌肉。
2. be introduced to. . . 初次接觸……
Those students were introduced to basic chemistry during the summer camp.
那些學生在夏令營期間初次接觸了基礎化學。
3. for this reason 因此
The hotel is close to the airport. For this reason, Alice booked a room there.
這間飯店離機場很近。因此，艾莉絲在那裡訂了房。

Taiwanese badminton veteran Chou Tien-chen on Friday advanced to the men’s singles semi-finals at the BWF World Championships in India, securing the second world championships medal of his career.
He was to play against Japan’s Kodai Naraoka after press time last night.
The 36-year-old world No. 6 defeated Indonesian rising star Alwi Farhan 21-15, 21-15 in 50 minutes to guarantee himself at least a bronze medal.
Photo: Reuters
Chou, who entered the match with a 2-1 career record against the world No. 12, used his defense and experience to neutralize Farhan’s attacks and claim his third win in their four meetings.
Chou after the match said that he took care of many of the details well during the match and was able to respond to many of the opponent’s tactics.
“His attacks were actually very sharp, but I went all out. I was able to defend successfully a lot of the time and maintained my advantage,” he said.
The opening game was closely contested from the start, with Chou winning a 60-shot rally to take his seventh point.
After Farhan scored three consecutive points, Chou capitalized on a series of unforced errors by the Indonesian to produce a 7-1 run and lead 14-11.
Leading 16-15, Chou was awarded a point when Farhan was called for serving above the permitted height. Farhan then lost four more points in a row as Chou closed out the game 21-15.
The second game remained tight until 11-11, when Chou began to take the upper hand as he switched up between the pace, drops and timely smashes.
Farhan was called for another service fault with Chou leading 14-12. The Taiwanese player later earned six match points with a body smash before securing victory when Farhan sent a net shot into the tape.
Chou said winning several long rallies shifted the momentum in his favor and boosted his confidence as the match progressed.
A regular BWF world championships quarter-finalist since making his tournament debut in 2013, Chou won his first medal at the event with a semifinal appearance in 2022.
“I won’t think about a particular goal,” Chou said. “I will just fight as hard as I can without any burden and leave everything to Jesus. I believe God will make the best arrangements.”
Meanwhile, Taiwan on Friday also secured a medal in men’s doubles as Lee Jhe-huei and Yang Po-hsuan upset world No. 2 Fajar Alfian and Muhammad Shohibul Fikri of Indonesia 21-19, 21-16.
The victory made Lee and Yang only the second Taiwanese pair to reach the men’s doubles semi-finals at the world championships, following Chen Hung-ling and Wang Chi-lin, who won bronze in 2018.
Lee and Yang were to face China’s Olympic silver medalists and world No. 3 pair Wang Chang and Liang Weikeng in the semi-finals last night after press time.

Vietnam’s rise could stumble on growth push
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-22
16:45:49 UTC
01:45:49 KST

Vietnam’s economy is on a roll. Hanoi, basking in the kind of praise that Southeast Asian peers won prior to the region’s financial crisis in the 1990s, wants still more rapid growth. However, leaders should be careful — such enthusiasm might well hasten the boom’s undoing.
Recent advances recall the glory days. In the second quarter, GDP climbed by more than 8 percent, easily exceeding forecasts. The closest to that, Malaysia, managed 6 percent. China, which for decades appeared largely insulated from business cycles, slackened to 4.3 percent. Vietnam’s government has its sights on a pace of at least 10 percent for the year.
Like the former Tiger economies that inspired it, Vietnam’s progress has been driven by breakneck industrialization and securing a lucrative niche in supply chains. Factories have churned apparel, furniture and electronics bound for shelves in the West, racking up enormous trade surpluses in the process. Tariffs on imports to the US were widely expected to slow things down. That has not happened, yet.
The performance has translated into meaningful gains in living standards. In July, the World Bank promoted Vietnam to the ranks of upper-middle income economies, joining Malaysia and Thailand. The Philippines also scored an upgrade. However, the pace at which Vietnam scaled the ladder is revealing. The bank had only elevated it to a lower-middle income economy in 2009.
It is reasonable to question how long a performance like this can be sustained. The more prosperous a country becomes, the harder it is to keep clocking up torrid rates of expansion, while a notable overheating would jeopardize financial stability and prod authorities to take firm steps to rein in activity.
Policy is increasingly geared to meet Vietnamese President To Lam’s objective of achieving high-income status by 2045, a century after the country declared its independence in the aftermath of World War II. Credit growth is running high: The central bank has set a target of 15 percent and has signaled it could indulge a greater amount. State spending is also being harnessed, with the budget deficit projected to widen. Managing this will be tricky. Officials want muscular growth, but do not want inflation to accelerate much beyond their target of 4.5 percent. Consumer prices jumped 5.6 percent from a year earlier in May, but have since increased at a more moderate pace. And they need to limit swings in the currency, which is allowed to fluctuate in a narrow band against the US dollar.
In an echo of how its neighbors ran into trouble during the Asian financial crisis, Lam also has his eyes on mega projects, including a US$2.5 trillion “master plan” to reconfigure large swathes of Hanoi. Ho Chi Minh City launched its own blueprint for a makeover. The risk is that such grand initiatives become an end to themselves. Waste and over-development are seldom far behind. While the ventures seem doable when times are good, they can sour when the economic and financial cycle turns. Recall the Vision 2020 program of former Malaysian prime minister Mahathir Mohamad, who in 1991 beseeched citizens to reach for a Swiss-style standard of living by the second decade of this century. Years of strong growth did follow, but so did ostentatious projects like the Petronas Towers and a cavernous airport that is too far from Kuala Lumpur and too thinly staffed. (Mahathir eventually acknowledged the 2020 goal would not be reached.)
Another danger lurks in the dependence of Vietnam’s export machine on the world’s biggest economy.
Last year, the trade surplus with the US ballooned to a record US$134 billion, an increase of more than one-fifth. the US’ shortfall with the country is the third largest after China and Mexico. The levies that US President Donald Trump announced in April last year were regarded as a steep challenge for Vietnam.
At that time, the White House also made clear it wanted to crack down on transshipments from China, a hard-to-pin-down practice where parts of a product are routed through Vietnam to the US with Vietnamese duties paid rather than the steeper charges applied to its northern neighbor. The Trump administration is now renewing its focus on constraining such traffic.
Hanoi cannot control Trump, but it can take care to avoid a hard landing. Relaxing credit guidelines would be risky, and the central bank should watch that activity does not become too hot. It is important policymakers realize that outperformance cannot last forever. Pushing growth above 8 percent for a considerable period might see the country gallop further up the development ladder, but it could also easily lead to an unacceptable build up of bad debts and an economy increasingly vulnerable to shocks. China offers a sobering lesson: After growth tore along in excess of 10 percent a year in the early 2000s, the nation’s model hit a wall.
“If Vietnam does achieve sustained 10 percent growth, it’s more likely to be a warning sign than a reason for celebration,” Capital Economics senior Asia economist Gareth Leather wrote last week.
Vietnam has done very well. It could do even better if it learns the lessons of its neighbors and shoots for something less than perfection.
Daniel Moss is a Bloomberg Opinion columnist covering Asian economies. Previously, he was executive editor for economics at Bloomberg News. This column reflects the personal views of the author and does not necessarily reflect the opinion of the editorial board or Bloomberg LP and its owners.
For the last 15 years, China has relied on gray zone operations to advance its territorial ambitions across Asia. And for 15 years, the US has struggled to respond. But the open door on which China has been pushing may finally be closing. Gray zone operations involve the assertive use of a variety of tools in ways that create conditions that can be described as neither peace nor war. Military forces might act provocatively — even dangerously — while carefully avoiding violence, whereas law enforcement employs nonlethal violence as a first resort. Such an approach creates difficult calculations for its targets.

Thousands of doses of Ebola vaccine arrive in DR Congo
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-22
16:45:46 UTC
01:45:46 KST

More than 16,000 doses of the Ervebo vaccine arrived in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DR Congo) late on Friday, as the country faces the deadliest Ebola outbreak in its history.
The DR Congo’s 17th Ebola outbreak, which has killed thousands of people, was declared on May 15, but is thought to have been spreading for several weeks prior. It has hit regions in the north and east where the presence of the state is weak, health infrastructure is largely lacking and myriad armed groups have roamed for decades.
The WHO on Thursday announced that DR Congo would receive a total of 70,000 doses of the Ervebo vaccine, produced in Germany.
Photo: AFP
The vaccine, developed by the pharmaceutical company Merck, is approved against the Zaire strain of the virus, but not against the Bundibugyo strain circulating in the country.
WHO experts still do not know whether Ervebo protects humans against the Bundibugyo strain, but early data, notably from animal trials, suggest it could offer some protection.
The Ervebo vaccine “has already been used several times, and in particular on a very large scale during the 2018-2020 outbreak,” Congolese Minister of Public Health Samuel Roger Kamba said.
He was speaking on the tarmac of Kinshasa airport, where a batch of 16,250 doses was delivered by plane.
Of the 70,000 doses made available to the DR Congo, 20,000 are intended for a clinical trial, and 50,000 for “frontline and health workers,” the WHO said.
The Ebola outbreak in the country has already caused 2,516 deaths among 5,290 confirmed cases, the latest data published by the Congolese authorities showed.
“[It] is growing exponentially,” UN Senior Ebola Coordinator Julien Harneis said.
This month, WHO vaccine experts recommended a full-scale human trial of Ervebo, the only existing approved Ebola vaccine, to see if it offered cross-protection against the Bundibugyo strain.
Two vaccines specifically targeting the Bundibugyo strain are in clinical trial phases: one is being developed by the US-based group Moderna, which uses mRNA technology, and the other by the UK’s University of Oxford.
An “rVSV Bundibugyo” vaccine, described by the WHO as “the most promising,” is to be developed by Singapore-based Hilleman Laboratories.

Ex-Chinese priest gets naturalized after decades
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-22
16:45:46 UTC
01:45:46 KST

A Catholic priest who was born in China and is now a US citizen has become a Taiwanese citizen after overcoming bureaucratic hurdles tied to his birthplace.
Xu Jingshan (徐景山), 67, who has been preaching in Taiwan for the past 20 years, said on Thursday that he first went to the US from China 33 years ago and later obtained US citizenship. He wrote off his household registration in China at the time.
He was assigned by the Catholic Church to Taiwan about two decades ago.
Photo: Hung Jui-chin, Taipei Times
Xu said that living in Taiwan without a national ID card had long caused practical inconveniences, such as difficulties in applying for a cellphone and obtaining a senior citizen card.
Upon learning about the government’s “Mackay Project” last year, he applied to become a naturalized Republic of China citizen for “making special contributions.”
His application was eventually approved by the Ministry of the Interior.
Because he was born in China, the National Immigration Agency (NIA) required that he provide documentation proving the cancelation of his Chinese household registration.
Xu said he had his relatives in China obtain the required documents from the local police station in his birthplace, but the NIA required the paperwork to be authenticated by Taiwan’s Straits Exchange Foundation.
However, the foundation only accepts notarized expulsion documents authenticated by Chinese notary offices, not expulsion documents directly issued by local police stations, Xu added.
A suspension in a Chinese notary office’s authentication service caused his application to stall, Xu said. In July, the office resumed the service, and his Taiwan ID card was ultimately issued.
During the process, he sought assistance from Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) Yunlin County Councilor Tsai Yueh-ju (蔡岳儒), who in turn enlisted the help of DPP Legislator Liu Chien-kuo (劉建國). His case was also submitted to the Executive Yuan and the Presidential Office.
Tsai said Xu had previously served in churches in Yunlin County, where he devoted himself to grassroots education and helped establish a day center for seniors at Lunbei Catholic Church.
Xu was transferred to the Church of the Good Shepherd six years ago and has made significant contributions to rural communities and disadvantaged residents, Tsai said.

TikTok to pay US$400m in privacy lawsuit
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-22
16:45:45 UTC
01:45:45 KST

TikTok has agreed to pay US$400 million to settle a lawsuit with the US Department of Justice over claims that the video-sharing platform contravened federal children’s privacy laws, the department announced on Friday.
Regulators around the world have been ramping up enforcement against social media companies that contravene laws about protecting children’s data, privacy and safety. Chinese company ByteDance — which sold off a majority stake of its US entity earlier this year to avoid a ban by the administration of US President Donald Trump — is also named as part of the settlement.
It has a 19.9 percent ownership stake in TikTok US, US media reported.
Photo: AFP
“Under the settlement, TikTok will pay $300 million immediately and an additional $100 million upon entry of an order vacating a prior consent decree entered against TikTok’s predecessor, Musical.ly,” the department said in a statement.
“[It is] one of the largest recoveries ever obtained” from a case involving the Children’s Online Privacy Protection Act (COPPA), the statement said.
The act bars Web sites from gathering the personal information of children younger than 13 without parental permission.
The justice department and US Federal Trade Commission jointly sued TikTok in 2024, alleging that it had placed the safety of millions of children in jeopardy by collecting their personal data without parental permission.
TikTok allowed children to use the app in addition to collecting and using personal data from young users without letting their parents know, they said.
Even accounts created in a “Kids Mode” intended for users younger than 13 gathered e-mail addresses and other personal information, the suit said.
In 2019, the US filed a COPPA lawsuit against an app called Musical.ly, which ByteDance bought in 2017 and then merged into TikTok.
TikTok did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
An ABC News report in May said that the Trump administration was considering using the funds for ongoing “beautification” projects, which have included resurfacing the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool, renovating the White House ballroom and building an arch.
It was not immediately clear what the settlement funds would be used for.
The US settlement comes amid a growing global crackdown on the video app.
Brussels began a probe into TikTok in 2024 under the Digital Services Act (DSA) — a content law and major weapon in the EU’s boosted legal armory that it has deployed to rein in Big Tech over the past few years.
Last month, the EU accused TikTok of failing to protect children through account settings that could expose them to risks such as cyberbullying and predatory behavior, putting the company at risk of a large fine.
Minors’ accounts should only be visible to those they have given permission to, the EU said.
Children ages 13 and over can use TikTok.
“A high level of protection should not be an opt-in; it should be the default,” European Commissioner for Digital and Frontier Technologies Henna Virkkunen said at the time.
Under the DSA, children’s account settings have, by default, the strongest safety and security protections.
“TikTok’s account settings fail to meet this standard, as they expose minors’ accounts and content too widely,” the EU said in its preliminary view.

Stars selling Greece to a new wave of US tourists
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-22
16:45:13 UTC
01:45:13 KST

The idyllic beaches of the Greek islands have long been a draw for European holidaymakers, but now a new wave of US tourists is waking up to their charms, driven by stars such as Madonna, Katy Perry and Justin Bieber.
Madonna celebrated her 68th birthday on Corfu, sharing a whirl of parties and boat trips against the backdrop of the island’s landscape with her 20 million Instagram followers — earning her rapturous thanks from Greek Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis.
Experts say the huge popularity of Christopher Nolan blockbuster The Odyssey would only fuel the trend — although holidaymakers would be hoping for an easier trip home than the one endured by Matt Damon’s eponymous hero.
Photo: Reuters
While Madonna partied in Corfu, singer Bieber took his family to the Peloponnese. Perry and her partner, former Canadian prime minister Justin Trudeau, sampled the delights of Mykonos.
All of them chronicled their holidays on social media, giving the Greek tourism industry a massive hit of free advertising.
“Celebrities are voting for the Greek summer,” public broadcaster ERT said on Friday, devoting a report to these stars from across the Atlantic.
The newspaper To Vima hailed this “new wave” which “helps raise the country’s international profile.” It cited British singer and actress Rita Ora, who shared her holidays with “her millions of followers” on social media.
Paris Tsartas, professor of tourism development at Harokopio University in Athens, said the deluge of celebrity endorsements gave Greece a powerful boost as a summer destination — particularly with the lucrative US market.
After a decade of financial woes following the debt crisis of 2009, and the devastation of the COVID-19 pandemic, Greece has pumped money into the sector, which accounts for about 30 percent of GDP, according to the Association of Greek Tourism Enterprises (SETE).
About 1.55 million Americans visited Greece last year. They represent the third-largest source of tourism income, behind Germans and Britons, with an average spend per tourist of 1,120 euros (US$1,308), the SETE said.
To answer growing demand, the main US airlines have significantly stepped up services, American Airlines increasing its total available seat capacity by 30 percent compared with summer last year. This year Greece has had its highest-ever number of direct flights, with 103 connections a week between Athens and the US.
Some of the new enthusiasm is driven by the phenomenon of “set-jetting” — people traveling to a destination after seeing it in a movie or TV series.
In a study for online travel giant Expedia, 13 percent of American travelers said they had booked a trip after seeing a destination on screen. Greece is well acquainted with the trend, after hit musical Mamma Mia, filmed on the island of Skopelos, triggered a jump in US visitors.
Tsartas predicted The Odyssey would have a similar impact. Key parts of Nolan’s film, recounting the travails of Damon’s Odysseus as he seeks to return home from the Trojan war to his wife Penelope, played by Anne Hathaway, were shot in the Peloponnese region of Greece. According to EasyJet Holidays, cited by ,
Bookings to Greece increased by 18 percent in the weeks following the film’s international release in last month, the Greek newspaper Kathimerini cited EasyJet Holidays as saying.
There is more small-screen exposure for Greece’s charms to come: Netflix had chosen the country for the sixth season of hit series Emily in Paris.
Lead actress Lily Collins and the rest of the production team were spotted this spring in Mykonos, Paros and Santorini.

Takaichi confronts her mentor’s mixed foreign policy
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-22
16:45:11 UTC
01:45:11 KST

Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi has inherited a lot of things from her mentor, the late prime minister Shinzo Abe: Her support base, conservative credentials, and even her favored slogan of “Japan is back.”
This is true of foreign policy, too. The sight of US President Donald Trump pulling the rug from under one of the US’ closest allies by ordering joint military drills with South Korea to be scaled back is but one reminder of the risks and rewards of Abe’s playbook in dealing with Washington. Russian President Vladimir Putin’s first-ever visit to islands controlled by Russia but claimed by Japan drags up the late premier’s biggest international failure. And talk of summits with North Korea recalls an event that made Abe’s early career, before turning to bitter regret.
Takaichi should put a little distance between herself and her mentor, and work through a new foreign policy to decide what should stay and what should go.
Illustration: Tania Chou
Start with Trump. Japan’s leader can learn many of the right lessons from his relationship with Abe. Whatever Trump’s true reason for abruptly hamstringing the South Korea drills — his affinity for North Korean leader Kim Jong-un, Seoul’s supposed failure to help with Iran or, as reports suggest, the slow pace of investment in the US — the move has startled Tokyo. Officials are no doubt concerned that as in 2018, Trump will increase demands on Japan ahead of the midterm elections.
One of Abe’s greatest diplomatic achievements was showing the world how to engage with the capricious president. He understood earlier than most that dealing with Trump meant flattery, copious reciprocity, big promises of spending, and a willingness to hold one’s nose. Despite periodic calls for higher spending on US troops and increased imports of US cars, Japan remains one of the few traditional allies that has largely dodged his opprobrium.
Takaichi has mostly followed that model, and for now Tokyo looks better placed than Seoul. She has turned US demands for investment into an opportunity to secure rare-earth and energy projects that will boost economic security. And she understands that Trump does not care if these do not add up to US$550 billion — the official amount Japan agreed to invest during last year’s tariff war — so long as he gets a good headline.
There are lessons to take away from Abe’s dealings with North Korea, too, amid reports that the US president is looking for another summit with Kim. As a young politician, Abe made his career with his hardline stance during then-Japanese prime minister Junichiro Koizumi’s historic summit with Kim’s father, Kim Jong-il, in 2002, which paved the way for the return of some of the Japanese citizens that North Korea had kidnapped.
Abe also sensibly avoided being used as a tool by Pyongyang, a concern that does not seem to bother Trump. Japanese media reported following his assassination four years ago that Abe had rejected a 2014 proposal to repatriate just two of the abductees, something he deemed a bad deal. Yet he was never able to secure his own visit to Pyongyang as leader, and was sidelined by Trump’s overtures to Kim.
Takaichi must similarly balance the risks of being bypassed against those of being used as a political pawn. Having taken up the abductee issue herself, a summit with North Korea would be a potential political win.
The question is leverage: This is a very different state from the impoverished one in 2002. Arms sales to Russia and crypto thefts leave Pyongyang with a diminished need for assistance. Without tangible results, Takaichi should not lend legitimacy to the Kim regime in return for a mere photo op.
For all his clear-eyed vision on China, Abe had a terminal blind spot for Putin. He burned years of political capital seeking a deal to reclaim the territory Moscow calls the southern Kurils and Japan dubs the Northern Territories, seized by the Soviet Union in the dying days of World War II. It was the unfinished legacy of his own father, Shintaro, who as foreign minister believed he could break the impasse.
Shinzo Abe held summits with Putin, seeking “hot-tub diplomacy” at an onsen resort, while officials from a northern prefecture gifted the Russian president an adorable dog. All to no avail, with Putin stringing Japan on so long that the dog died of old age last year.
Any attempt to restart such talks should stay dead, too, but there are concerning signs that some around the prime minister want to return to this failed strategy, and re-engage with Moscow. Takaichi is notably the only G7 leader yet to hold a bilateral meeting with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy. She must not make the same mistake Shinzo Abe did: allowing the ghosts of the past to dictate the present.
Shinzo Abe’s skill was in understanding that personal relations could create room for Japan where it might be militarily outmatched, but his mistake was sometimes to confuse relationships with actual results. Takaichi needs to know the difference.
Indeed, it is important to know when to change tactics when needed. That is what Shinzo Abe, at his best, would have done.
Gearoid Reidy is a Bloomberg Opinion columnist covering Japan and the Koreas. He previously led the breaking news team in North Asia, and was the Tokyo deputy bureau chief. This column reflects the personal views of the author and does not necessarily reflect the opinion of the editorial board or Bloomberg LP and its owners.
For the last 15 years, China has relied on gray zone operations to advance its territorial ambitions across Asia. And for 15 years, the US has struggled to respond. But the open door on which China has been pushing may finally be closing. Gray zone operations involve the assertive use of a variety of tools in ways that create conditions that can be described as neither peace nor war. Military forces might act provocatively — even dangerously — while carefully avoiding violence, whereas law enforcement employs nonlethal violence as a first resort. Such an approach creates difficult calculations for its targets.

Arsenal on Friday made the perfect start to their English Premier League title defense with a stylish 3-0 win against Coventry City in the opening game of the season.
Mikel Arteta’s side brushed aside promoted Coventry in emphatic fashion at the Emirates Stadium, underlining their determination to retain the title.
Kai Havertz struck early in the first half, and Bukayo Saka doubled the lead before Martin Odegaard netted after the interval to complete Arsenal’s masterclass.
Photo: Reuters
The Gunners have not successfully defended the English title since the 1930s, but Arteta insisted this week his players are hungry for more silverware.
Just 89 days after rounding off their title-winning campaign with a 2-1 victory at Crystal Palace in May, the champions showed no sign of being sated by that long-awaited triumph as they put Coventry to the sword.
The only downside for Arsenal was the realization they have to wait 10 days for their next game at Aston Villa.
Worryingly for Arsenal’s rivals, they are only getting stronger, and new signing Ezri Konsa was given a warm welcome when he was presented to fans before kick-off.
The England defender completed his ￡51 million (US$69.6 million) move from Villa earlier on Friday and could make his debut against his old club on Aug. 31.
Greek winger Christos Tzolis dazzled on his first league start for Arsenal after his close-season move from Club Brugge.
Fellow new signing Bruno Guimaraes was hardly missed after being sidelined by an injury sustained in last weekend’s Community Shield win over Manchester City.
Coventry were playing their first Premier League game since 2001 after winning the Championship last season to end their long exile from the top-flight.
Having spent a season in the fourth tier, plunged into administration and twice been forced to ground-share away from Coventry in the 25 years since they were last in the Premier League, the return of Frank Lampard’s side was a feelgood moment.
However, Arsenal had no room for sentiment as they dispatched Coventry in merciless style.
In their first home league game since being crowned champions last season, Arsenal strode onto the pitch with the acclaim of the sell-out 60,000 crowd ringing in their ears.
The party atmosphere created by Arsenal’s jubilant fans in north London was a fitting backdrop to a swaggering performance.
Tzolis, who provided two assists in the Community Shield, nearly bagged his first Arsenal goal in the opening minutes, firing just over from Odegaard’s pass.
He went close again moments later with a close-range effort that was cleared off the line by Bobby Thomas.
It was no surprise when Arsenal took the lead in ruthless fashion after 15 minutes.
Coventry defender Milan van Ewijk surrendered possession carelessly on the right flank and Riccardo Calafiori pounced, whipping in a cross that Havertz met with a clinical low strike from just inside the penalty area.
Arteta’s rampant team scented blood and went for the kill in the 23rd minute.
Rice and Odegaard exchanged passes to work the ball out to Tzolis, whose cross was pushed out by Coventry keeper Carl Rushworth into the path of Saka for a simple close-range finish.
Coventry had been reduced to helpless bystanders by Arsenal’s ceaseless pressing and clever movement.
If it was not already over, Odegaard put the result beyond doubt in the 49th minute.
Saka and Ben White teamed up to rip through the Coventry defense before Odegaard’s miscued shot from 10 yards scuffed past Rushworth’s weak attempted save.

The challenges of Bilingual 2030
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-22
16:45:10 UTC
01:45:10 KST

Jye Smallwood’s article on English-medium instruction (EMI) raises important questions about how Taiwan’s bilingual ambitions are being translated into classroom practice. In particular, he draws attention to a distinction that can easily become blurred: EMI is a teaching context, not a language-teaching method, and teaching a subject through English creates challenges that English proficiency alone cannot solve.
When assessing the challenges of Bilingual 2030, it is tempting to ask whether the policy is succeeding or failing. As a language educator, I wonder if there is a more constructive question: What has the experience taught us?
Language teachers navigate a similar problem every day.
During communicative fluency activities, students inevitably make errors. A teacher might be tempted to interrupt every mistake immediately. However, doing so can quickly disrupt the communication the activity was designed to develop.
Experienced teachers often do something different: We listen.
We observe what students are trying to accomplish. We notice which problems occur repeatedly, which interfere with communication and which are simply momentary slips. Then, after the activity, we address the patterns that matter most.
This is known as delayed correction. It is not about ignoring mistakes. It is about gathering enough evidence to make the subsequent intervention more useful.
Perhaps Bilingual 2030 has reached a similar point.
After years of implementation across Taiwan’s schools and universities, the policy has generated considerable experience with bilingual classrooms, EMI, teacher development and different approaches to supporting students. Inevitably, not everything has worked as intended. That is concerning, but it is also something valuable to learn from.
Smallwood’s observations highlight one important pattern. Deep subject knowledge and strong English do not automatically answer the pedagogical questions that arise when teaching a subject through English. Knowing economics, engineering or history and creating the conditions for students to learn those subjects are different forms of expertise.
This does not mean turning university professors into language teachers. As Smallwood said, EMI is a teaching context, not a language-teaching method.
However, that context places particular demands on teachers’ professional judgement: how to make complex ideas accessible without diminishing them, how to determine whether students have understood and how to create opportunities for students to engage with the subject rather than simply listening to it in another language.
Language education has wrestled with similar questions for decades. Communicative approaches shifted attention from simply presenting language toward creating conditions in which learners use it. The methods cannot simply be transplanted into an economics or engineering lecture, but some of the underlying lessons might transfer.
Effective teaching begins not only with what we intend to teach, but with careful attention to how these students are actually learning it.
The same principle can help with Bilingual 2030.
Delayed correction works because the teacher does not react to every error in isolation. The teacher observes long enough to identify patterns and then decides which interventions are most likely to improve the next attempt.
Taiwan has years of experience from which to do the same.
An initiative as ambitious as Bilingual 2030 was always going to test assumptions and reveal approaches that needed refinement. Identifying those weaknesses does not mean declaring the entire policy a success or a failure.
It provides an opportunity to ask which patterns have emerged, where students and teachers are succeeding, where they continue to struggle, and what support would make the greatest difference.
The value of delayed correction is not that mistakes become acceptable. It is that accumulated experience allows the teacher to respond more intelligently.
Bilingual 2030 has given Taiwan that experience. The important question is what we choose to learn from it.
Daniel Eyrich is director of English Studies at CenYing English in Keelung and has more than 15 years of experience in English language teaching, assessment and teacher development in Taiwan.

Average household income up 3.3%
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-22
16:45:10 UTC
01:45:10 KST

Average total household income in Taiwan was NT$1,529,000 (US$ 48,009) last year, up 3.3 percent from a year earlier, the latest data from the Directorate-General of Budget, Accounting and Statistics (DGBAS) showed.
Median disposable household income last year was NT$1,018,000, up 3.4 percent from a year earlier, the data showed.
Employee compensation was the main source of household income, although significant regional differences were evident, DGBAS said.
Graphic: CNA
Hsinchu City and Hsinchu County had average total household incomes of NT$2,042,000 and NT$2,007,000 respectively, the highest in Taiwan, it said.
They were followed by NT$1,857,000 in Taipei, NT$1,557,000 in Taoyuan and NT$1,506,000 in New Taipei City, it said.
Employee compensation accounted for more than half of household income in Taiwan’s six special municipalities, Hsinchu County and Hsinchu City, DGBAS said.
Hsinchu City and Hsinchu County reported significantly higher average household incomes, mainly because the high-paying technology sector dominates their economies, resulting in higher salaries, overtime pay and year-end bonuses, it said.
Other important sources included interest income, investment income and other property income, including rental income, DGBAS said.
Average household property income in Taiwan was NT$76,000 last year, with Taipei highest at NT$180,000, or nearly 10 percent of average household income in the city, it said.
The figures show that property income is a particularly important component of household income in Taipei, although DGBAS cautioned that its data do not sufficiently disaggregate rental income from other forms of property income to identify the main source.
Hsinchu City last year reported average household property income of NT$131,000, making it the only other administrative division where property income exceeded NT$100,000, it added.
Taiwanese stocks surged last year, especially shares in artificial intelligence companies, but gains from buying and selling stocks or funds are excluded from the agency’s household-income calculations because they are treated as changes in wealth rather than income, DGBAS said.

The eight-time NBA All-Star is to lead a TAT All-Star team against a Kings All-Star squad in the “Kings Heart Classic” at Xinzhuang Gymnasium in New Taipei on Sept. 13, the club said in a news release.
The full rosters — which would include basketball players and entertainers — would be announced before the game, the Kings said.
Photo: AP
“My time in Taiwan was special. Taiwanese fans are the most passionate in the world. I still remember that atmosphere,” Howard, 40, was quoted as saying in the statement.
“I’m looking forward to coming back, and especially to doing something for Taiwan’s stray dogs. See you in Xinzhuang on Sept. 13,” he added.
Part of the proceeds from the event would be donated to PACK Taiwan, an animal welfare organization, to improve shelter care and support the adoption of stray dogs, the Kings said.
Before the charity game, the Kings are to play a friendly against the Macau Black Knights, with Howard serving as a guest commentator. A fan meet-and-greet with Howard is to be held between the two games.
The former NBA center became one of Taiwan’s most prominent foreign athletes after joining the Taoyuan Leopards in the now-defunct T1 League for the 2022-2023 season following 18 seasons in the NBA.
Howard averaged 23.2 points, a league-leading 16.2 rebounds and five assists in 20 games for the Leopards. His debut drew a sellout crowd of 15,000 and about 160,000 viewers on the league’s YouTube livestream.
He returned to Taiwan in July 2024 to play for the Taiwan Mustangs in the TAT, a league in which he said he had an ownership stake.
Howard again highlighted his ties to Taiwan during his September last year induction speech at the Naismith Basketball Hall of Fame, saying that basketball had allowed him to form connections around the world and mentioning his efforts to establish a league in Taiwan.
Howard, nicknamed “Superman,” won an NBA championship with the Los Angeles Lakers in 2020 and was named the league’s Defensive Player of the Year three times.

Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-22
16:45:07 UTC
01:45:07 KST

Taiwan’s proposed defense budget for next year sends a signal that should resonate with the White House, which has urged allies and partners to increase defense spending, a US academic said Friday.
The Cabinet on Thursday approved the central government budget proposal for next year, which would allocate NT$1.1225 trillion (US$35.2 billion) for defense, equivalent to 3.01 percent of GDP.
Michael Hunzeker, an associate professor at George Mason University who studies Taiwanese defense issues, said the proposed budget was a “very positive development” that showed that President William Lai (賴清德) remained committed to keeping defense spending above 3 percent of GDP and on track to reach 5 percent by 2030.
Photo: Cheng-Chia Huang, Reuters
Given the White House’s emphasis on urging allies and partners to increase defense spending, Hunzeker said that the proposal should send a signal that would be welcomed by the White House.
“It should likewise send a clear signal to Beijing that its increasingly aggressive actions have not caused the Lai administration to back down on its national security promises,” he added.
Hunzeker said a growing defense budget should give Taiwan’s Ministry of National Defense and armed forces more resources to acquire better and more appropriate weapons, ammunition and spare parts, expand rigorous and realistic training, enhance resilience efforts, and attract and retain personnel for mission-critical frontline combat units.
“Of course, this proposal is just the start of a long process. Potential obstacles and challenges remain,” he added.
Hunzeker said that the proposal still needs to be reviewed by the legislature and could face scrutiny similar to that faced by this year’s budget, which lawmakers only passed this month.
He also pointed to opposition parties’ pushback against Lai’s proposed eight-year special defense budget, saying further scrutiny could be expected as parties prepare for upcoming elections.
A US Department of State spokesperson welcomed Taiwan’s proposal to increase defense spending to more than 3 percent of GDP, saying that it demonstrated Taiwan’s resolve to improve its self-defense capabilities.
The spokesperson said the US supports Taiwan’s acquisition of critical defense capabilities “consistent with the Taiwan Relations Act and more than 45 years of commitment across multiple US administrations.”
The spokesperson added that “the threat Taiwan faces from China has grown considerably.”

S Korean container to sail Arctic route
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-22
16:45:05 UTC
01:45:05 KST

South Korea was yesterday to send its first trial container through the Arctic, as the Middle East war rattles global shipping, while environmental groups warned that the route could accelerate polar ice melt.
The Middle East conflict has roiled global shipping, sending governments and shipping firms scrambling to seek alternative routes.
Sailing from Busan New Port, container ship PanStar Acro would sail to Europe via the Arctic, testing whether a route opened by melting sea ice could be commercially viable.
Photo: AFP
“The ship will depart at 8pm today unless there are unforeseen circumstances, such as bad weather,” a South Korean Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries official said.
The ship would leave for Felixstowe in the UK, Rotterdam in the Netherlands and Gdansk in Poland before returning, with the voyage expected to take about 45 days, the ministry said.
The voyage follows that of the Chinese container ship Dubai Tower, which left the eastern port city of Ningbo for Europe this month, heading north through the Bering Strait before turning west along Russia’s Arctic coast.
The usual maritime route between Asia and Europe runs through the Suez Canal, but traveling through the Arctic could cut the journey by about 7,000km and about 10 days, the Korea Institute for International Economic Policy said.
South Korean Vice Minister of Oceans and Fisheries Nam Jae-hon said the Arctic route was “bound to become an alternative” to Middle Eastern shipping lanes — as geopolitical risks and technological advances make it increasingly competitive.
Arctic University of Norway political science professor Marc Lanteigne said the voyage — coming soon after Dubai Tower began its own Arctic journey — showed that the Northern Sea Route was becoming normalized as a “secondary maritime transit corridor.”
A successful voyage would demonstrate South Korea’s interest in “developing alternative shipping sea lanes,” he said, adding that it could fall behind as Chinese firms expand regular services through the increasingly viable Arctic route.
Some experts warned that South Korean ships using the Arctic route could risk breaching Western sanctions on Russia, as they would receive Russian navigation and weather services involving payments, albeit small ones.
The South Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs declined to comment about the concerns involving Russia.
The oceans ministry said this week that “consultations with key relevant countries and agencies” have been completed to “implement administrative procedures necessary” for the voyage.
University of Oslo Korean studies professor Vladimir Tikhonov said: “strictly speaking, US and EU sanctions are not international law, unlike UN sanctions.”
“And with continued uncertainty in the Middle East — itself driven in part by US actions — South Korea may have few alternatives if the Arctic route proves economically viable,” he said.
Lanteigne said China’s Northern Sea Route ambitions were more politically driven than South Korea’s, with Beijing viewing the polar regions as “strategic new frontiers,” raising Western security concerns.
Meanwhile, environmental groups warned growing traffic along the shorter route could accelerate Arctic sea ice loss already driven by global warming. Major carriers including CMA CGM, MSC and Hapag-Lloyd have pledged to avoid Arctic shipping routes.
The route is believed to be accessible only during the time of year when the ice is melted enough to allow transits without icebreakers.
“The Northern Sea Route has become increasingly viable as the Arctic warms about four times faster than the global average, leading to a sharp decline in sea ice,” South Korean environmental group Paran Ocean Citizen Science Center said in a statement last year. “But making the route commercially viable would require further warming, putting the policy at odds with efforts to combat climate change.”

Tropical depression threatens torrential rain
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-22
16:45:01 UTC
01:45:01 KST

The Central Weather Administration (CWA) yesterday forecast heavy rain for southern Taiwan today, saying tropical depression TD22 would strengthen southwesterly winds and bring more downpours.
The CWA said that in addition to torrential rain in southern Taiwan yesterday, mountainous areas in central and southeastern Taiwan also saw heavy rainfall, while northern and northeastern mountain areas were hit by short-duration downpours amid intense afternoon thunderstorms.
Tainan had experienced continuous rain since Friday night, with Yongkang District (永康) recording more than 132mm of rainfall in three hours and Rende District (仁德) nearly 100mm over the same period, the CWA said.
Photo courtesy of the Central Weather Administration
By 3:20pm yesterday, Pingtung County’s Wandan Township (萬丹) had recorded 281mm of accumulated rainfall, the highest nationwide, followed by Majia Township (瑪家) with 263mm. Kaohsiung’s Siaogang District (小港) had recorded 254.5mm and Linyuan District (林園) 242mm, while Tainan’s Gueiren District (歸仁) had recorded 237.5mm.
The CWA at 5pm yesterday activated enhanced operations for large-scale or severe rainfall as stronger southwesterly winds approached Taiwan. It said the most intense rainfall was expected from today through early Tuesday.
Southern Taiwan could see extremely heavy rain during that period, while Chiayi and eastern Taiwan could see localized extremely heavy rain and central Taiwan localized heavy rain, it said.
In its latest 24-hour rainfall forecast, covering 8pm yesterday to 8pm today, the CWA said mountainous areas of Chiayi County, Kaohsiung and Pingtung were expected to meet rainfall thresholds used in decisions on suspending work and classes.
As of yesterday afternoon, TD22 was about 350km east of Taiwan. Although the Japan Meteorological Agency had upgraded the system to Typhoon Gaenari, the CWA continued to classify it as a tropical depression, saying its circulation and convection remained relatively weak.
The CWA said TD22 was expected to move northwest before turning west toward the Chinese coast. Even if it strengthens into a typhoon, its forecast track would take it more than 300km north of Taiwan, making a sea warning unlikely, although the system is expected to strengthen the southwesterly flow and bring heavier rain to southern Taiwan.
Typhoon Saudel was about 2,600km east of Taiwan at 2pm yesterday, with maximum sustained winds of about 137kph and gale-force winds extending an average of 180km from its center, the CWA said. It could strengthen into a strong typhoon today.
Saudel is forecast to move northwest before turning west-northwest toward the Ryukyu Islands, reaching the area on Wednesday or Thursday. It is then expected to slow and could track farther west, bringing it somewhat closer to Taiwan, although its path remains uncertain, the CWA said.
The typhoon’s outer clouds and circulation could bring increased rainfall to northern Taiwan on Friday and Saturday, with rain also possible in central and eastern Taiwan, it added.

Two US tanker aircraft leave Bulgaria a month after deployment upset Iran
Aug 22 - Two U.S. tanker aircraft have left Bulgaria’s Bezmer air base, Bulgaria's defence minister said on Saturday, nearly a month after their deployment in the Balkan country angered Iran.
The United States, which has been at war with Iran since February 28, requested their temporary deployment under an agreement governing the joint use of military facilities.
Iran said at the time that their deployment would constitute complicity in "aggression and war crimes", a charge that Sofia dismissed.
The two U.S. Air Force KC-135 planes left Bulgaria on Friday, Defence Minister Dimitar Stoyanov told reporters.
The U.S. authorities could not be immediately reached for comment.
The deployment of the aircraft, approved by Bulgaria's parliament on July 22, led to protests by nearby residents who feared the planes would be attacked by Iranian missiles and drones.
Stoyanov said all the aircraft's flights during their temporary deployment had been training missions over allied countries and that Bulgaria had "no information about direct threats to our national security."
"We are working in full coordination with the U.S. government and had prior information, which is why all our decisions were well-founded," he said. REUTERS

Three South African universities ranked among world's top 500
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-22
23:43:16 CST
00:43:16 KST

CAPE TOWN, Aug. 22 (Xinhua) -- Three South African universities have been ranked among the world's top 500 higher education institutions in the 2026 Academic Ranking of World Universities (ARWU), local media reported on Saturday.
The University of Cape Town was ranked the country's top university, placed in the 201-300 range of the latest ranking. The university's performance was driven largely by its strong output of published and highly cited research, particularly in scientific fields.
The University of the Witwatersrand, in Johannesburg, ranked second nationally in the 301-400 range, while Stellenbosch University was placed in the 401-500 range.
Several other South African universities were also included among the world's top 1,000 institutions.
The ARWU, a global indicator of university performance published annually by China-based ShanghaiRanking Consultancy, uses six objective indicators, including Nobel Prize and Fields Medal winners among alumni and staff, highly cited researchers, papers published in the journals Nature and Science, publications indexed in major citation databases, and per capita academic performance.
The ranking covers more than 2,500 universities, with the top 1,000 published.
Harvard University retained the world's top position, followed by Stanford University and the Massachusetts Institute of Technology. U.S. universities dominated the top 100, with 37 institutions, while China had 16, led by Tsinghua University, ranked 18th in the world.
ARWU was first published in 2003 by the Center for World-Class Universities at Shanghai Jiao Tong University and has been published by ShanghaiRanking Consultancy since 2009. ■

Roundup: Polish experts see growing potential for AI cooperation with China
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-22
23:43:14 CST
00:43:14 KST

WARSAW, Aug. 22 (Xinhua) -- As artificial intelligence (AI) moves rapidly from laboratories into factories, hospitals and classrooms, its expanding applications are creating new opportunities for scientific and technological cooperation between China and Poland.
Polish experts see growing potential for deeper China-Poland AI cooperation, citing the complementary strengths of China's mature industrial ecosystem and broad application market and Poland's expertise in mathematics, engineering and basic research.
Katarzyna Kaniewska, an official with the Foreign Cooperation Office of the Polish Chamber of Commerce, said China and Poland can deepen cooperation in healthcare, climate-related services and education.
Both China and Europe face population aging and declining birth rates. AI can help ease pressure on healthcare systems by handling some routine examinations, laboratory tests and administrative tasks, allowing medical professionals to devote more time to work requiring human judgment, Kaniewska said.
It can also support climate monitoring and early warning, while serving as an auxiliary tool for teachers and students, she added.
For companies, cooperation can help develop AI solutions tailored to local market demand. For researchers, it can expand existing personnel exchanges into joint work in basic research, said Roman Szewczyk, director of the Systems Research Institute of the Polish Academy of Sciences.
Cezary Blaszczyk, director of the Department of International Cooperation at the National Centre for Research and Development of Poland, said Chinese and Polish researchers have shown a strong willingness to work together and that the potential for AI cooperation is substantial.
According to Szewczyk, basic research should remain central to AI cooperation. His institute has trained doctoral students from China, and he hopes collaboration can expand beyond personnel exchanges to joint fundamental research.
Krzysztof Pyrc, president of the Foundation for Polish Science, said the potential of research cooperation with China remains underestimated by some scientists abroad.
Greater links among universities, research institutes, funding bodies and enterprises can help convert complementary strengths into concrete results, he said.
For China and Poland, robotics cooperation can bring together AI algorithms, sensors, control systems, mechatronics and manufacturing expertise, creating opportunities in areas ranging from industrial automation to medical and elderly-care services.
The benefits, however, will extend beyond robotics.
The same model -- joint research followed by local testing and adaptation -- can be applied in healthcare, climate services and education. It can also make AI tools more accessible to Polish small and medium-sized enterprises, helping them improve efficiency and develop new products and services.
Blaszczyk emphasized that companies generally approach cooperation in practical terms, focusing on technological strengths, product competitiveness and market demand.
Such an approach can help turn scientific collaboration into viable products and services with wider economic and social value.
"I hope the challenges brought by AI development can be addressed through bilateral cooperation, and that AI can benefit humanity and create more possibilities for future cooperation," said Blaszczyk. ■

Domestic production, regional integration urged to build resilient health economy in East Africa
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-22
23:43:00 CST
00:43:00 KST

Guests attend the 13th East African Health Federation Conference and International Exhibition in Addis Ababa, the capital of Ethiopia, Aug. 21, 2026. (Photo by Michael Tewelde/Xinhua)
ADDIS ABABA, Aug. 22 (Xinhua) -- Experts and policymakers on Friday called for building a resilient regional health economy in East Africa, through expanded domestic medical manufacturing, enhanced public-private partnerships, and accelerated cross-border integration.
They made the call during the 13th East African Health Federation Conference and International Exhibition, which opened Friday in Addis Ababa, the capital of Ethiopia, with the aim of building resilient health systems across the region and beyond.
The three-day high-level gathering, running until Sunday, has brought together more than 2,000 delegates from over 20 countries, including decision-makers, private sector leaders, medical supply manufacturers, experts, and digital health innovators, under the theme "Resilience: Building the East African Health Economy."
Addressing the conference, Workneh Gebeyehu, Executive Secretary of the Intergovernmental Authority on Development, an East African bloc, said that health sovereignty represents "the absolute bedrock of national sovereignty." He noted that historical vulnerabilities to global supply chain disruptions must be converted into enduring regional industrial strength and healthcare resilience.
"Healthcare is a strategic, high-growth economic driver. It creates skilled jobs, attracts global investment, accelerates industrial manufacturing, and safeguards our most precious asset: our human capital," said Gebeyehu.
Calling for the structural alignment of the public and private sectors to address regulatory and trade barriers, he emphasized the necessity of deploying long-term capital into pharmaceutical manufacturing, digital health networks, and cold-chain infrastructure to establish a unified East African health economy.
According to the organizers, deliberations at the three-day conference are strategically structured around four core pillars: excellence in health service delivery, local manufacturing, investment financing, and regional integration.
Ethiopia's Deputy Prime Minister Temesgen Tiruneh called for a fundamental shift in the region's health sector approach toward greater local production. He noted that building public health resilience must progress beyond merely recovering from health crises, focusing instead on anticipating challenges, effectively responding to emergencies, and turning healthcare into economic strength.
"Resilience cannot mean simply recovering from the last crisis. It must mean preparing for the next one by building our capacity to act and turning health from a story of vulnerability into a source of African strength," Tiruneh said.
He highlighted the East African country's ambition to become an African hub for specialized healthcare and medical tourism, mainly through expanded domestic production of essential pharmaceuticals, diagnostics, and medical equipment, while deepening critical public-private partnerships.
Experts and policymakers at the conference stressed that building robust regional health systems requires more than public financing, emphasizing the critical need to put in place a thriving, well-governed private sector that partners with governments to invest, manufacture supplies, and mobilize capital.
Echoing this sentiment, Ethiopia's Health Minister Mekdes Daba highlighted that public health challenges, including supply chain disruptions and climate change, extend beyond borders and demand collaborative solutions. She noted that strengthening local research and development as well as medical manufacturing remains essential to minimizing vulnerabilities to future global crises.
As East Africa's flagship healthcare event, the conference has also attracted more than 80 exhibitors from Africa and beyond to showcase medical products, services, technologies, and innovations, serving as a platform to connect solution providers with healthcare decision-makers, according to the organizers. ■

KINSHASA, Aug. 22 (Xinhua) -- The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) has surpassed 5,300 confirmed cases and 2,550 deaths, as a senior United Nations official warned that the country's deadliest-ever Ebola epidemic is "growing exponentially" and outpacing the response.
The DRC has recorded 5,375 confirmed cases and 2,557 deaths across six provinces as of Thursday, according to the latest figures released Saturday by the country's public health authorities. The overall case fatality rate stood at 47.6 percent.
A total of 1,167 patients have recovered.
Briefing reporters Friday from Bunia, capital of Ituri province, UN Senior Ebola Coordinator Julien Harneis warned that the outbreak was "growing exponentially," with half of all deaths recorded in just the previous 20 days.
"The epidemic is spreading to an area that is bigger than France," Harneis said, warning that the outbreak was "growing faster and wider than the Ebola response."
The epidemic, declared by the DRC government on May 15, has already become the deadliest Ebola outbreak in the country's history and the second-largest on record globally, behind only the 2014-2016 West Africa epidemic.
Harneis said responders were operating under "brutal" conditions, citing insecurity, poor roads, attacks on frontline workers and health facilities, as well as weak basic services and difficulties in moving funds into affected areas.
Three months into the outbreak, 160 healthcare workers have contracted Ebola and 43 have died, he said. Ambulances have been burned or stoned and healthcare facilities attacked in some affected communities.
Funding shortages have also emerged as a major concern. "We're only covered for the next weeks, and very soon funding will run out," Harneis said, calling for immediate international support.
"Every delay in funding and implementation makes this epidemic more deadly, more difficult to stop and more expensive," he warned.
Harneis said humanitarian organizations operating in the region had lost more than 30 percent of their capacity amid cuts to aid funding over the past two years, although UN agencies, the DRC authorities and humanitarian partners continue to scale up disease surveillance, treatment, safe burials and community engagement.
The latest warning comes as international partners move to reinforce the response. The World Health Organization said earlier this week that 70,000 doses of the Ervebo Ebola vaccine had been approved for immediate release to the DRC, including 20,000 doses for a Phase 3 clinical trial and 50,000 for frontline and health workers.
A first batch of 16,520 doses of the Ervebo vaccine arrived late Friday in the capital Kinshasa. ■

Heavy rain began shortly after the race ended. "The three of us were just talking - if there was one more lap, it could potentially have been a very different end to the race, so I was glad the rain came when it did. I had a pretty good start," Russell said. ■

BEIJING, Aug. 22 (Xinhua) -- China's Ministry of Water Resources on Saturday activated a Level-IV emergency response to flooding in Guangdong, Guangxi and Hainan, as Typhoon Narra is forecast to bring torrential rains to southern China.
From Aug. 22 to 24, Narra, the 19th typhoon of this year, will bring heavy to torrential rainfall across southern and western Guangxi, Guangdong and Hainan, with some areas expecting extremely heavy downpours, the ministry said.
Water levels are forecast to rise in several rivers in Guangxi, Guangdong and Hainan. The Zuojiang and Mingjiang rivers, tributaries of the Yujiang River, as well as some small and medium-sized rivers in the rainstorm-hit areas may see floods above warning levels.
The ministry has urged local water resources departments to closely monitor the typhoon's development, strengthen rain and river monitoring, forecasting, and early warning, while ensuring the scientific operation of water conservancy projects.
It stressed the importance of preventing mountain torrents and small and medium-sized river floods, ensuring reservoir safety during the flood season, and implementing safety measures for tourists and construction workers.
Authorities should dynamically update high-risk area catalogs, evacuate residents from hazardous areas in a timely manner, and make every effort to safeguard people's lives and property, the ministry added.
Also on Saturday, the State Flood Control and Drought Relief Headquarters and the Ministry of Emergency Management jointly activated a Level-IV emergency response for typhoon and flood control in southeastern Fujian Province.
China has a four-tier flood-control emergency response system, with Level I being the most severe. ■
