U.S. Marine Corps accepts first Ancillary Surface Craft prototype
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-22
08:38:42 UTC
17:38:42 KST

- The Marine Corps Warfighting Laboratory completed technical acceptance of its first Ancillary Surface Craft prototype, built by Birdon America under a 2024 contract.
- The 150-foot landing craft can carry 46 tons of cargo and 40 Marines and is rated for Sea State 5 operation, surviving up to Sea State 7.
The U.S. Marine Corps Warfighting Laboratory has completed technical acceptance of the first Ancillary Surface Craft prototype, moving the roughly 150-foot vessel into a new phase of testing at Quantico, Virginia, the laboratory said in a release.
The ASC is a roll-on/roll-off landing craft designed to carry personnel, equipment, and fuel directly onto unimproved shorelines, delivering what the Marine Corps calls the “last tactical mile” of logistics support. The laboratory said the craft can transport up to 46 tons of cargo and 40 combat-loaded Marines. It is rated for full operation in Sea State 5 and designed to survive conditions up to Sea State 7.
The craft is equipped with forward-looking sonar intended to let operators navigate uncharted, shallow littoral waters and assess beach gradients before landing.
The Marine Corps awarded the ASC contract to Birdon America, the U.S. arm of Australian shipbuilder Birdon, in 2024. Birdon partnered with C&C Marine and Repair in Belle Chasse, Louisiana, to build the vessel, with construction beginning in 2025 at C&C’s facility near New Orleans. Birdon has said the ASC design, which it also refers to as the Ancillary Surface Craft-Medium, was built for rapid, automation-driven production intended to shorten the time needed to build each craft.
“Achieving technical acceptance is a crucial first step in our rigorous testing regimen,” said Aaron Hatfield, Maritime Program Manager, Science and Technology Division, U.S. Marine Corps Warfighting Laboratory.
“This validation assures that the craft’s advanced systems and robust design are ready for MCWL to begin hands-on technical experimentation, ensuring we can meet the extreme operational demands of the Indo-Pacific theater.”
The ASC now enters limited technical assessments, in which Birdon America craft masters and engineers will work alongside Australian Army crewing support under Marine Corps Warfighting Laboratory oversight. The laboratory said the craft will initially be operated by a hybrid crew pairing Marines with contracted mariners as the Marine Corps trains its own personnel toward independent operation of small surface craft.
The ASC is intended to complement the Medium Landing Ship, a larger amphibious vessel the Marine Corps and Navy have been developing to move forces between islands. The Medium Landing Ship program has faced repeated delays, and the Marine Corps has described the ASC and similar smaller craft as part of an interim “bridging strategy” to sustain distributed forces in the Pacific while that program continues. Where the Medium Landing Ship moves forces at a larger scale, the ASC is built with a shallow draft meant to reach landing sites beyond the reach of bigger vessels, including shorelines without ports, piers, or causeways.
“To support Expeditionary Advanced Base Operations (EABO), our forces must remain highly mobile and sustained without relying on fixed, vulnerable ports,” said Col. Kenny Jones, Science and Technology Division Director at the Marine Corps Warfighting Laboratory.
“This prototype allows MCWL to immediately execute hands-on experimentation, test tactical concepts, and put real hardware in the hands of Marines. By exploring the ASC’s traditional bow-first beaching physics alongside other experimental platforms, we are actively reducing programmatic risk and perfecting the requirements for the future naval fleet.”
Expeditionary Advanced Base Operations is the Marine Corps concept for positioning small, mobile units at temporary locations across contested maritime areas, including islands in the Pacific, to support sea denial and fleet sustainment missions. The concept relies on units that can move between locations without depending on fixed infrastructure that would be vulnerable to attack.
The Marine Corps has ordered two ASC prototypes from Birdon under the current contract. Upcoming testing phases will evaluate force protection and self-defense configurations for the craft, whose primary mission remains logistics and maneuver rather than direct combat.

Defense Forces confirm destruction of Russian Su-24M at Saky airfield
Ukrinform
    Ukraine’s Defense Forces have confirmed the destruction of a Su-24M aircraft and four pieces of Russian airfield support equipment in temporarily occupied Crimea on August 20.
    According to Ukrinform, the General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine reported this on Facebook.
“On August 20, following the strike on the Saky airfield (Novofedorivka, temporarily occupied territory of the Autonomous Republic of Crimea), Ukraine’s Defense Forces destroyed a Su-24M aircraft and four pieces of the enemy’s airfield support equipment,” the statement said.
Operations against key Russian facilities are ongoing.

As previously reported by Ukrinform, the General Staff released the results of the strike on the Primorsko-Akhtarsk airfield in Russia’s Krasnodar Krai.

Akhmat Kadyrov's name to be forever inscribed in history of Russia — Putin
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-23
08:20:25 UTC
17:20:25 KST

MOSCOW, August 23. /TASS/. The name of the first president of the Republic of Chechnya, Akhmat Kadyrov, is forever inscribed in the history of Russia, President Vladimir Putin said in a video message on the occasion of the 75th anniversary of the birth of Akhmat-Khadzhi Kadyrov.
"Today, August 23, would have marked the 75th anniversary of the birth of Akhmat Kadyrov - the first president of the Chechen Republic and a Hero of Russia," the president stated.
"His name has been enshrined forever in the country’s history, and for us he will remain a person whose strength of spirit and unconditional love for his people could overcome evil and make a step to returning peace to the ancient Chechen land," Putin emphasized.
According to him "It was the faith in his people and its future that determined the path in Akhmat Kadyrov’s life, helped him make the most important, very conscious decisions during the dramatic and hard period that Chechnya was going through in the 1990s."
"At the most difficult juncture, when the society was split and divided and the republic was virtually in ruins, Akhmat-Khadzhi took on a tremendous responsibility. His position based on his deep conviction was clear-cut: Chechnya’ destiny is inseparable from that of Russia, and his main objective was not only to stop the fratricidal conflict, but also to put an end to it forever, to revive Chechnya, preserve the entire North Caucasus and to put up a reliable barrier to the aggression of international terrorism supported from abroad by the enemies of Russia’s multiethnic people."
The Russian president pointed out that "Akhmat-Khadzhi was a courageous man, who understood very well how hard the burden was and what risks he was going to take on."
"Being a truly spiritual leader, he managed to lead the people and do everything to bring back peace to the long-suffering Chechnya and confidence about the future to its residents," according to Putin.
"His word and influence rescued many people from the traps set by radicals and false preachers whereas his consistent position delivered a crushing blow to the pseudo religious propaganda and attempts to impose extremist ideology in Chechnya alien to the republic and turn religion into an instrument of statehood destruction," the Russian president noted.
"I remember our meetings and conversations. I remember how he explained to me why he had decided to head Chechnya. ‘Today, he said, we need people ready to sacrifice everything, and if necessary, their lives for the sake of their people’."
"Regretfully, these words were prophetic. He did not manage to accomplish much of what he had planned, and there can be neither forgiveness nor oblivion for that crime, committed despicably and cynically on Victory Day which is sacred to our country," Putin said.
"Akhmat-Khadzhi always believed that Chechnya would be thriving and prosperous. I am confident that he would have been proud of the present-day republic, its transformation and dynamic progress. He would have been proud of how worthy his course is continued by his adherents, above all by his son," the Russian president added.
Akhmat Kadyrov became president of the Chechen Republic in October 2003. On May 9, 2004, he was killed in a bomb blast at a stadium in Chechnya’s capital Grozny during the World War II memorial victory parade.

Ozon Warehouse in Orenburg Region Hit in Drone Attack, Governor Says
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-23
08:14:41 UTC
17:14:41 KST

The governor of Russia's Orenburg region said on Sunday that two industrial facilities were hit by drone debris, including a warehouse owned by Ozon, a major Russian online retailer.
Governor Yevgeny Solntsev said that the Russian Defense Ministry had repelled six drones over the region, adding that no one had been injured. He did not name the second damaged facility.
Ozon, Russia's second-largest online retailer, said in a statement on Telegram that the company had evacuated more than 300 people and that work at its Orenburg region logistics center had been halted.
On Saturday, Ukrainian drones hit an Ozon logistics center in Russia's Samara region in a strike which was the first on Ozon. The strike follows weeks of drone attacks targeting its larger rival Wildberries, which Ukraine has cast as part of a wider campaign against economic infrastructure underpinning the Russian war in Ukraine.
Russia's Defense Ministry said it downed 328 Ukrainian drones overnight.
